title: Selling Property in India by an NRI: Tax & TDS Demystified
description: Capital gains tax implications for an NRI selling property in India remain the same, irrespective of whether the buyer is a resident Indian or another NRI. Ta.

faq.q: What is the primary difference in tax implications for an NRI selling property to a resident vs. another NRI?
faq.a: The primary difference lies in the TDS deduction and compliance process for the buyer, not the NRI seller's capital gains tax liability. The NRI seller's tax on capital gains remains the same regardless of the buyer's residency.

faq.q: Does an NRI buyer need a TAN to deduct TDS when buying from another NRI?
faq.a: Yes, an NRI buyer is legally obligated under Section 195 of the Income Tax Act to deduct TDS when purchasing property from another NRI and must obtain a Tax Deduction Account Number (TAN) to do so.

faq.q: Can an NRI seller avoid TDS deduction completely?
faq.a: No, TDS deduction is mandatory on property sales by NRIs. However, an NRI seller can apply for a Lower Deduction Certificate (Form 13) under Section 197 to reduce the TDS rate to their actual tax liability or even to nil if eligible.

faq.q: How does indexation benefit an NRI seller?
faq.a: Indexation allows the NRI seller to adjust the original cost of acquisition for inflation, significantly reducing the taxable Long-Term Capital Gains and thus the overall tax liability.

faq.q: What happens if the buyer fails to deduct TDS?
faq.a: If the buyer (resident or NRI) fails to deduct or deposit TDS, they can be held liable for the unpaid tax, along with interest and penalties, by the Income Tax Department.

faq.q: Can I repatriate all the sale proceeds immediately?
faq.a: Repatriation of sale proceeds is subject to FEMA guidelines. Generally, an NRI can repatriate up to USD 1 million per financial year from their NRO account, after all taxes are paid and necessary documentation (like Form 15CA/15CB) is submitted.

based_on.title: Selling property in India by an NRI to another NRI vs. an Indian resident: Tax implications and TDS
